headline: Council approved first passage of mobile home park rent moratorium ordinance 5-2, but failed to waive rules for final passage.
summary: The Council held a public hearing on extending a moratorium ordinance on rent increases for mobile home park lots, effective September 29, 2026. Many residents and park owners spoke for and against the extension. The Council approved first passage of the ordinance by a 5-2 roll call vote, but a motion to waive council rules to allow final passage the same night did not pass, so the final passage motion was not brought forward.
decisions: Approved first passage of the Moratorium Ordinance regarding Rent Increases for Lots in Mobile Home Parks, effective September 29, 2026, by a 5-2 roll call vote.
Motion to waive Section 3 of the Rules Governing the City Council to allow final reading the same night failed 4-3, since a 2/3 majority was required.

decision_evidence.quote: That the proposed Moratorium Ordinance regarding Rent Increases for Lots in Mobile Home Parks, to be effective September 29, 2026, receive first passage by a roll call vote. Passed - Vote 5 – 2 (Councilors Longchamps and Martel opposed.)
To waive Section 3 of the Rules Governing the City Council and to allow for final reading at this time. Did Not Pass - Vote 4-3 (Councilors Longchamps, Noble and Martel opposed.)

CITY OF LEWISTON 
 
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 25, 2026 
 
SPECIAL MEETING HELD IN THE COUNCIL ROOM AT 6:00 P.M. 
 
THE HONORABLE CARL L. SHELINE, MAYOR, PRESIDING. 
          
PRESENT: Mayor Sheline, Councilors Nagine, Longchamps, Harriman, Noble, Chittim, and 
Martel, City Administrator Bryan Kaenrath and Deputy City Administrator Brian O’Malley. 
Absent/Excused: Councilor Roy. Note – The City Charter permits the Mayor to cast a vote in the 
absence of a City Councilor.  
 
Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag. 
 
PUBLIC HEARING AND FIRST & FINAL PASSAGE FOR AN EXTENSION OF 
THE MORATORIUM ORDINANCE REGARDING RENT INCREASES FOR 
LOTS IN MOBILE HOME PARKS 
Mayor Sheline opened the public hearing.  
 
Eryn Soule, Ward 5 – Rent control caps what a property owner can charge does not reflet the 
costs of operating the property. When revenue is frozen, owners may cut back on maintenance, 
close the mobile home park, or sell. A rent control cap sends a wrong message and shows the 
city is not business friendly. 
 
Lisa Jones, Ward 2 – Submitted a Freedom of Access to learn how the need for this meeting 
came about. City Council is in charge, not City Attorney. A special City Council meeting was 
requested a while ago to address gun violence, and it was denied. The new Council President 
promised transparency, but it has not been demonstrated yet. Owners of mobile home parks have 
been very clear about the impact if this ordinance goes through. Lewiston residents want a safe 
city; this should be your priority. 
 
Janet Beaudoin, Ward 2 – Speaking on behalf of a constituent who is opposed to the moratorium 
extension. Parks are privately owned businesses. Make financial and legal details public and 
make sure the park owners and residents receive a fair process.  
 
Craig Saddlemire, Ward 4 – Chair of Housing Committee, speaking as one member of the 
committee. He noted the Committee did not request the extension of the moratorium which was 
noted in the agenda material.  The Committee is continuing work on the ordinanc e. 
 
Erica Robert, Ward 7 – Realtor, was representing Sunset Gardens, a mobile home park that was 
for sale. There was a potential pending sale, but the prospective buyer withdrew when the lot rent 
ordinance was announced and devalued the park by 26%.  Rent freezes do not address the 
problem of housing which is the high cost of maintaining a property and have a negative impact 
on marketing.Should focus on increasing affordable housing options. Please reject proposal. This 
is a private business sector that should not be regulated. If park owners cannot afford to maintain 
the area, the parks will fall into disrepair.  
 
Laurie Horton, Ward 2 – Park owner, was scheduled to sell August 1 and leave for cross-country
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 25, 2026 
                             
2 
 
trip, all fell through when the rent control ordinance was proposed. Park owners are local and 
have kept past increases to the minimum to support the residents. State implemented new laws in 
September and these restricted the amounts lot rents can increase annually. Do not need to 
extend the moratorium, city does not need to be involved in this issue because the state is already 
regulating it. The Council failed to do due diligence. The proposed limit is not sustainable. 
 
Dash Padham, Ward 3 – Time to get more information and more presentations on this topic 
before doing a final passage right away. Another six-month moratorium puts both park owners 
and tenants in an unfair holding pattern. Recently resigned from Housing Committee because of 
disagreements with direction of committee on this topic. 
 
John Gerry, Ward 6 – Resident of Fox Run mobile home park. The previous speakers stated the 
passage of this will give the wrong message to investors. There have been no investments in new 
parks since 2003. Ordinance says owners can set market rate, whatever the market will tolerate. 
Approval extension of moratorium to avoid a gap in coverage, that gap will create legal issues.  
 
John Horton, Ward 2 – Understand need for affordable housing. The Governor’s Office sent this 
ordinance to all towns, and the Maine Labor Climate Council told the city mistruths about the 
topic. No one asked the obvious question – is an ordinance needed in Lewiston? No park has 
been predatory in nature, we have opened our books to the Housing Committee to review. The 
proposed ordinance will be hard to manage and cause implementation issues for park owners. 
Have run his parks for 18 years. Or may have to close the parks, subdivide into housing lots and 
storage unit lots. No resident has been harmed so far but park owners have been. 
 
Chris Saroie, Ward 1 – Owner of Sunset Gardens mobile home park.  There seems to be a 
misconception that park owners are flush with cash, rich and greedy. This is not the case. All 
profit is reinvested into park improvements and maintenance.  In five month s of meetings, the 
question has never been asked if rent stabilization is necessary. Believes the proposed ordinance 
was not created to assist residents but a political endeavor instead. 
 
Nicole Penfield, Regional manager for Beauvita Communities – they operate three parks in 
Lewiston. Asked Council to seriously consider what private businesses are allowed to earn. 
Purchased Country Lane and Stetson Brook in 2024. They have issued one rent increase per year 
averaging $37. The average lot rent in these communities is $473 per month. This is compared to 
$1650 for a 2 bedroom apartment rent for one month. Parks maintain private roads, water and 
sewer infrastructure, electrical systems, drainage, landscaping, trash removal and common areas. 
Work with residents though payment plans if needed.  A private business cannot absorb ev ery 
financial issue however. Capping revenue does not cap expenses. Have land available but will 
not expand if ordinance is approved to limit the potential income.  
 
Katie Lauzie, Lewiston resident – Housing Committee member but comments are her own. 
Believes housing is a human right. The Committee has worked for months to seek a balance. We 
have not looked at data from current park owners. The data shows an affordability problem. It 
does not support the claim that park owners are the cause of the problem. Park rents are fair and 
within market rate. This ordinance could put parks at risk and therefore the housing of all of the 
tenants at risk as well. Ordinance will have a chilling effect on real estate purchases. Urged 
Council to vote against continuation of moratorium.
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 25, 2026 
                             
3 
 
Michelle Ames, Brookside Mobile Home Park owner – The state law allows towns to create 
ordinances if the state law language does not address the local issues.  She believes the state law 
does address issues in Lewiston and a local ordinance is not necessary. The lot rent increases in 
her parks average $15.72 a year. Expenses such as insurance, worker’s comp, wages, etc have all 
increased sharply. Park has 30 lots and their assessment just increased by a million dollars. 
Create a problem to subsidize lot rents for tenants who need it, because not all park residents 
need it. 
 
Matt Agren, Ward 4 – Urge Council to vote against.  Sets a horrible precedent that the city 
regulates the profits for private businesses. This undermines small business owners. The rents in 
Lewiston are not off the chart. 
 
Adam Cranse, Assistant Regional Manager for Beauvita Community. The time under the 
moratorium was to answer two questions – whether rents in Lewiston are fair and whether park 
owners can still earn a fair return on their investment. This process has not answered either as of 
yet.  No data showing residents are being overcharged, no evidence that language already in 
state law are not working. Do not extend moratorium. 
 
Mayor Sheline then closed the hearing. 
 
 
VOTE (1) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
That the proposed Moratorium Ordinance regarding Rent Increases for Lots in Mobile Home 
Parks, to be effective September 29, 2026, receive first passage by a roll call vote. 
 
Passed - Vote 5 – 2 (Councilors Longchamps and Martel opposed.)  
 
 
VOTE (2) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Nagine: 
 
To waive Section 3 of the Rules Governing the City Council and to allow for final reading at this 
time. 
 
Did Not Pass - Vote 4-3 (Councilors Longchamps, Noble and Martel opposed.)  (Note – Since 
this motion was to waive the Rules, a 2/3 majority – minimum of 5 affirmative votes – was 
required for passage. As such, this motion failed.) 
 
Since the motion to waive the Rules and allow for a final passage at this time did not pass, the 
motion for final passage was not brought forth. 
 
 
VOTE (3) 
Motion by Councilor Chittim, seconded by Councilor Martel:
CITY COUNCIL  AUGUST 25, 2026 
                             
4 
 
To adjourn at 7:07 P.M.  Passed - Vote 7-0 
 
A true record, Attest: 
 
 
 
Brian T. O’Malley  
Deputy City Administrator 
Lewiston, Maine
